title: BADGE: BADminton report Generation and Evaluation with LLM

paper.authors: Chiang, Chao, Wang, Wang, Peng (National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University)
paper.other_artifacts: Rally-level source data derived from ShuttleSet (Wang et al. 2023); a GitHub Pages demo reproduces the generation and evaluation prompts in the browser

dependence.note: gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 is both the writer of the reports under test and the G-Eval-style judge that produces every number in Tables 1 and 2; the human evaluation (Table 3) is the external reference against which the judge's validity is assessed. Report generation and scoring are therefore two dependent uses of the same dying snapshot.

claim.statement: With the CSV input type and the Chain-of-Thought prompt on 10 ShuttleSet matches, reports written by gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 are scored by the same model (G-Eval-style, four criteria, 1-10) at 8.6 coherence / 9.4 consistency / 8.2 excitement / 9.1 fluency, average 8.825, above GPT-3.5-turbo-0125 reports (8.625) and above human-written reports (7.925) on every criterion (Table 2), while human judges rank the same reports GPT-4 8.225 > human 7.450 > GPT-3.5 6.350 (Table 3) and the GPT-4-to-human correlation is only r = 0.333, i.e. the LLM judge shows the G-Eval self-preference for machine-written text.
claim.metric: Mean GPT-4 evaluation score per criterion (coherence, consistency, excitement, fluency; integer 1-10, one call per report per criterion), averaged over the 10 matches, and their 4-criterion average. Secondary: Pearson r between the GPT-4 and human evaluation scores (0.333).
claim.original_source: Paper Table 2 (GPT-4 evaluation by writer), Table 3 (human evaluation), Table 1 (GPT-3.5 writer across data types and ICL; its CSV+CoT row 8.625 is identical to the Table 2 GPT-3.5 row, which is how we identify Table 2 as the CSV+CoT condition), Sec. 4.5 for the correlation.

protocol.model_usage_verified: yes, dated snapshot in both paper and code. Sec. 3.2 names GPT-4-turbo-2024-04-09; code/generation/GPT-4.py and all three scripts in code/evaluation/ hardcode model = gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09. No alias inference needed.
protocol.endpoint: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions (openai SDK, single user message, one call per report and per criterion)
protocol.prompt_source: prompt/generation/CSV+CoT.txt (writer; the paper prints only its opening lines) and prompt/evaluation/{coherence,consistency,excitement,fluency}.txt (judge: task introduction + criterion definition + three fixed evaluation steps + report + an evaluation form asking for scores only). The evaluation steps were auto-generated once by GPT-4 per the G-Eval recipe and are frozen in these files.

params.temperature: not set (API default 1.0) - matches the original scripts, which pass only model and messages
params.note: unset temperature means the writer and the judge are both stochastic; with 10 matches per cell the run-to-run spread is large and must be reported

protocol.n_items_note: per seed: 10 generation calls (10 matches x CSV+CoT, GPT-4 writer) + 120 judge calls (3 writers x 10 matches x 4 criteria). The GPT-3.5 writer arm is not regenerated (gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 is dead, shut down 2026-03-26); its released reports and the human reports are judged as-is.
protocol.samples_note: 1 per item per seed, 3 seeds (the paper ran one pass); at temperature 1.0 the seeds are the main variance estimate
protocol.evaluation: Score extraction from free text: the released judge outputs are sometimes a bare integer, sometimes 'Coherence: 9' plus an explanation, sometimes several paragraphs with the score only at the end. The repo ships no parser or aggregation script, so the card must add one (documented as a pipeline paraphrase, not a prompt change) and archive the raw judge text.
protocol.environment: python + openai (environment.yaml / requirements.txt, unpinned). One-line path fix needed: the generation scripts write to generation/<game>/<model>/, the evaluation scripts read report/<game>/<model>/.

artifacts.prompts_path: prompt/generation/ (8 files: CSV|QA x zero-shot|one-shot|few-shot|CoT) and prompt/evaluation/ (4 criteria)
artifacts.data_path: CSV/<game>/CSV.txt and QA/<game>/QA.txt (the 10 pre-formatted match inputs, English, ~6.0 kB and ~2.9 kB per match) built by code/data/CSV+QA.py from data/<game>/set*.csv (ShuttleSet rally records); generation/<game>/{GPT-4,GPT-3.5,human}/ holds the released reports (170 files)
artifacts.eval_path: code/evaluation/{GPT-4,GPT-3.5,human}.py; released judge outputs in evaluation/<game>/<writer>/<report>/<criterion>.txt (680 files). No scorer or table-building script is included.
artifacts.data_license: repo MIT; the rally data derive from ShuttleSet (public research dataset, separate terms); the 10 human-written reports were collected from the Internet by the authors (third-party news text redistributed in the repo)
artifacts.redistributable: code and derived CSV/QA inputs: yes (MIT). Human-written reports: treat as non-redistributable third-party text; keep them inside the L1 archive only as prompt inputs.
artifacts.notes: Item-level original outputs ARE released, which is rare. We re-aggregated them without any API call: the human row (7.5 / 8.9 / 6.8-6.89 / 8.5, avg 7.933) and the GPT-3.5 row (8.4 / 9.2 / 8.0 / 8.9, avg 8.625) reproduce Table 2 exactly, but the GPT-4 writer row aggregates to 8.40 (coherence 8.40, consistency 8.00, excitement 8.20, fluency 9.00), not 8.825. Two released consistency judgements for GPT-4 reports are 3 and 4 (one file contains no number at all), so the published GPT-4 row cannot be rebuilt from the released files.

blockers: The released judge outputs do not reproduce the published GPT-4 row: our parse gives avg 8.40 vs Table 2's 8.825 (human and GPT-3.5 rows match exactly), so the Table 2 GPT-4 cell corresponds to a different judging pass or a score-extraction rule that is not documented.
Decoding parameters are unset (temperature 1.0), so both writer and judge are stochastic on n = 10 matches; the 0.20 gap between the GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 rows is within plausible run-to-run noise.
The GPT-3.5 writer arm (gpt-3.5-turbo-0125) is dead, so that row of Table 2 can only be re-judged from the released reports, never regenerated.
Table 3 (human evaluation) and the r = 0.333 correlation need human raters and cannot be re-executed; only the GPT-4 side of the comparison is reproducible.
Repo path mismatch (generation/ written, report/ read) and no aggregation script: a small harness wrapper is required and must be logged as a pipeline paraphrase.

baseline_alive.purpose: live baseline (P0) in both roles, writer and judge; cheap (about USD 8 for the full three-seed design)

successors: gpt-5.6-sol (vendor-designated replacement for gpt-4-turbo on the OpenAI deprecations page)
dead_comparators_not_runnable: gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 (writer arm, shut down 2026-03-26; released reports are reused as fixed inputs)
arms.design_note: Writer and judge can be varied independently. Default: same snapshot in both roles, as in the paper. A successor-judge / live-writer cell isolates whether the self-preference effect follows the judge or the writer.

budget.assumptions: 3 seeds x (10 generation + 120 judge) calls. Generation: ~1,830 input tokens (CSV.txt averages 5,995 chars plus the 543-char CoT prompt) and ~560 output tokens (released CSV+CoT reports average 2,149 chars). Judging: ~1,100 input tokens (criterion prompt ~2,200 chars + report) and ~250 output tokens (the judge writes a score plus an explanation despite the scores-only instruction). Repo README's own figures for one pass were USD 2.50 generation and 2 x USD 3.00 + USD 0.37 evaluation.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1. Primary number: the 4-criterion average for the gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 writer under the same-model judge (median of 3 seeds) against 8.825. Survival = median inside the bootstrap 95% CI over the 10 matches of the original AND the direction holds: GPT-4 reports >= GPT-3.5 reports > human reports on the average (the paper's self-preference claim). Partial = level moves outside the CI but the LLM-over-human ordering survives. Death = human-written reports are scored at or above the LLM-written ones, which would undo the paper's central observation.
judgment.notes: Ordering, not level, is the load-bearing part, and with n = 10 matches at temperature 1.0 the CI is wide (the released item scores range 3-10 on consistency). Report the writer effect (GPT-4 vs GPT-3.5 reports, 0.20 apart) as fragile by default. A second, cleaner test holds the reports fixed (re-judging the released GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and human reports) so that only judge drift is measured; the discrepancy we found between the released judge outputs and Table 2 makes that fixed-report arm the more informative one.

decisions_2026_09_19.primary_arm: full protocol: regenerate the GPT-4 reports with prompt/generation/CSV+CoT.txt, then judge all three writers' reports with prompt/evaluation/<criterion>.txt. Answers user_check 1.
decisions_2026_09_19.secondary_arm: judge-only on the released reports (reports frozen), which isolates judge drift. The GPT-3.5 and human judge calls are identical in both arms and are issued once, so the secondary arm adds only 10 matches x 4 criteria x seeds calls on the released GPT-4 reports.
decisions_2026_09_19.comparison_targets: the published Table 2 value 8.825 is primary; the 8.40 re-aggregated from the repo's own released judge outputs is reported alongside and is the like-for-like target of the secondary arm. Answers user_check 2.
decisions_2026_09_19.score_parser: bare integer, else the last criterion-labelled number (markdown bold and a trailing 'Score' tolerated), 1-10 enforced, unparseable = missing; logged as a pipeline paraphrase. Answers user_check 3.
decisions_2026_09_19.table1_grid: skipped (user_check 4 declined): only the CSV+CoT condition of Table 2 is run.
decisions_2026_09_19.budget: per-paper cap USD 15, split writer 3 / judge 12; --dry-run 2026-09-19 estimate 510 calls (30 writer + 480 judge) at 3 seeds, ~517k input / ~68k output tokens, ~USD 7.21.
decisions_2026_09_19.check_result_2026_09_19: the primary parser reproduces the Table 2 GPT-3.5 row exactly (8.625) and gives 8.400 for the GPT-4 row (published 8.825). The human row gives 7.947 with one judge reply dropped, and exactly the published 7.925 under a criterion-stem sensitivity variant that reads that reply's renamed criterion ('- Excitiveness: 6') and changes only that 1 of the 120 cells. NOTE: this card's artifacts.notes figure 7.933 for the human row is reproduced only by a markdown-blind parser that additionally drops '- **Fluency**: 9', and that parser breaks the GPT-3.5 row (8.606); all three parsers are computed in runs/W4400103831/environment_check.json so the figure stays traceable. The card's criterion values for the human row (7.5 / 8.9 / 6.8-6.89 / 8.5) are correct; their average is 7.925-7.947, not 7.933.

user_checks: Re-run both stages (regenerate the GPT-4 reports, then judge all three writers), or hold the released reports fixed and re-run only the judge? Cost is nearly identical; only the fixed-report arm isolates judge drift.
Judge Table 2 against the published 8.825, or against the 8.40 we recomputed from the repo's own released judge outputs (report both, pick the primary)?
Accept our score parser (bare integer, else the last criterion-labelled number in the text; unparseable = missing) as the documented pipeline paraphrase?
Include the 8-cell Table 1 grid as a fixed-report judge-only arm (+80 calls per seed, ~+USD 2)?
domain_notes: BADGE is a two-phase framework: rally-level ShuttleSet records are flattened into a 6-column CSV (or a Q&A rendering) and given to the LLM writer, then a G-Eval-style judge scores the report on four criteria. Table 2 compares the same 10 matches across three writers, and the paper's contribution beyond the sports application is the confirmation of G-Eval's preference for machine-written text: the LLM judge places GPT-3.5 reports above human reports while human raters place them last (Table 3). The workshop paper has 2 citations and reports no statistical test, so this card carries the ordering, not the decimals. No Tier B config exists for this paper (data/tierA_pass2_cards.csv in_tierb = False); this card upgrades the triage plan from a prompt-level replay to a repository-based re-execution: full prompt files instead of the abridged paper text, the 10 identified matches with their pre-formatted CSV inputs, and the released reports and judge outputs as the frozen comparison set.
